notes:
Summary: Auric Bay builds a multitenant contact center routing platform used by retail and telco customers (US + EU). They want real-time agent assist (streaming suggestions and tool-call triggers) that survives 10x daily spikes. POC scope: 10 agent seats with simulated bursts up to 20k RPS across 3 regions, streaming suggestions delivered within 50ms p95 token latency and suggestion finalization <200ms.

Meeting highlights: 
- 2026-02-12 discovery call (FF id ff_2026-02-12_auric-support-poc) — product + infra. They care most about latency and deterministic behavior during bursts. Quote from Head of Platform: "If assist feels slow it creates more work than it saves."
- 2026-02-20 security kickoff — IT requested SOC2 + KMS + retention controls; asked about EU residency for subset of transcripts.
- 2026-03-04 demo — showed streaming LM with tool-calling prototype; SE asked for per-token cost estimates and fallback plans.

Technical constraints & notes: 
- Must support streaming token-by-token suggestions to agent UI via websocket/SSE; end-to-end SLO target: p95 token latency <= 50ms within North America region for 1k concurrent agents, with capacity to burst to 10k concurrent for sales events.
- Tool-calling: must trigger internal ACD/CRM RPCs safely — need signed request headers and audit trail for each tool call.
- Guardrails: policy layer for hallucination mitigation + constrained tool invocation list. Prefer model-level filters + post-generation deterministic checks.
- Models: prefer open Llama-2 style families but willing to evaluate Redwood-verified variants; interested in quantized 4-bit options to reduce memory footprint on Dedicated pools.
- Routing: prefer smart routing by policy (latency first for premium customers, cost-forced fallback to smaller model for bulk tier).
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, session pinning for agent-specific contexts.
- Observability: need token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency traces, and correlation IDs included in logs for incidents.

Commercial: Auric Bay expects TCO comparison vs in-house GPU infra. They are open to Dedicated reserved pools for predictable sections and Hosted for overflow. POC will include pricing estimate for sustained vs burst traffic.

Next steps checklist: 
- Redwood and Auric infra teams to run 10-seat POC load test (target week of 2026-03-15).
- SE (Ethan) to provide kernel/quantization recommendations and expected p95 numbers for candidate models.
- Security to confirm SCIM/MFA integration timelines and data residency controls (IT to provide EU customer list).
- Draft contract with burst pricing addendum once POC metrics validated.
